A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same DAT research. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across the extensive appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original DAT classification, generation, robustness, counterfactual, and ablation results. Table 16 additionally reports results across five independent runs.

after.justification: v3 retains the original DAT experiments in Tables 1–2 and the appendices, including the five-run results now reported in Table 19.

M1.justification: The combined robust-classification and BCE objectives, PGD contrastive sampling, ancestral sampling, two-stage training, normalization handling, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The revised regularization argument changes the method's justification, not its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, auxiliary OOD data, corruption benchmarks, and counterfactual scenarios. The L-infinity experiment and supplementary OOD evaluations already appear in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the matched main and appendix tables, including JEM, SADA-JEM, RATIO, standard AT, EGC, and specialized generative models. Newly discussed counterfactual methods, including DVCE, are not added to the reported evaluations.

E3.justification: Training configurations, augmentation, attack budgets, checkpoint selection, sample counts, and evaluation metrics are retained. Tables 3–6 and the generation settings in v2 Table 10 versus v3 Table 8 match; relocated supplementary experiments retain their protocols.

E4.justification: Component, augmentation, OOD-data-size, loss-weighting, corruption, norm-generalization, and gradient-stability analyses retain the same comparisons and evidence. The removed training-cost chart redisplayed information still available in the cost analysis and table.

E5.justification: v2 Table 16 and v3 Table 19 report identical means and standard deviations across five independent runs with different random seeds, including zero divergences. No statistical reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: All 19 matched tables retain their numerical entries, and retained plots and qualitative samples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports the same ConvNeXt-L DAT FID of 3.29, IS of 310.2, and robust accuracy of 56.40% in both versions.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix A.2's Taylor expansion and cross-entropy gradient decomposition are replaced by v3 Appendix A.3's operator-norm argument, per-class spectral-norm bounds, and attack-budget scaling derivation. The retained optimal-logit proposition also receives revised reasoning about adversarial cross-entropy and compatibility with the marginal-energy constraint.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and claims about high-resolution scaling, combined generation and robustness, and competitiveness with specialized generative models.

C2.justification: The central regularization explanation shifts from confidence-weighted gradient penalties and alignment terms to spectral-norm control of every class gradient, with new attack-budget and GAN-regularization implications. Section 4.3.2 adds an intrinsic-explainability rationale, while the distribution discussion qualifies uniformity as equal unnormalized density on the support.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix B.2 and Table 7 shorten the hardware-conversion documentation and omit v2 Table 17's explicit explanation that ADM-G and LDM-4-G throughput estimates were converted from reported A100 measurements. Other implementation settings remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds Roth et al. (2020) and Yoshida and Miyato (2017) for the norm-based analysis, plus Boreiko et al. (2022) and Augustin et al. (2022) for counterfactual positioning. The new DVCE discussion emphasizes DAT's independence from external generative and auxiliary classifier models.

P1.justification: The single supplementary appendix is reorganized into Theory & Method, Training & Evaluation, and Results & Analyses. Related theory and gradient evidence are combined, trade-off discussion is merged with loss-weighting analysis, and the main results narrative and counterfactual explanation are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: Appendix displays are extensively regrouped: the gradient plot joins the theory, training curves receive a separate page, and generation grids are redistributed. Duplicate figure numbering is corrected, Figure 1 is relocated, and v2's training-cost breakdown chart is removed while its tabulated values remain.

improvement.justification: Clearer appendix organization and corrected figure numbering improve navigation. However, v3 Appendix A.3 invokes an equivalence stated for logit-norm losses without establishing its applicability to DAT's cross-entropy objective, leaving the revised theoretical justification unresolved. Omitting baseline throughput-estimation provenance also reduces transparency. With empirical evidence unchanged, these mixed effects prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
